title: Beef Shin Ragu
subtitle: Slow-braised Italian beef ragu with pasta
excerpt: Beef shin braised for two and a half hours in wine and tomato until it falls apart into a rich, deeply savoury ragu. Tossed with wide pasta and finished with no more than a little parmesan. One of the most rewarding things you can make on a weekend.
sourceNotes: Slow-braised beef ragu is a staple of central and northern Italian cooking. Beef shin is the traditional cut for this style of ragu due to its high collagen content, which breaks down during long cooking to give the sauce its characteristic body.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the ragu separately from the pasta. Reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: The ragu doubles well with no change to technique.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The ragu is better on the second day. Make it the day before and reheat before serving.

content.text: The beef shin must be browned very well before braising. Colour at this stage is flavour. Do not rush or crowd the pan.

items.prepNote: wide pasta such as pappardelle or tagliatelle

content.text: Pat the beef shin dry and season well with salt on both sides.
Heat the oil in a stockpot over a high heat. Brown the beef shin for 4 minutes each side until deeply coloured. Remove and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and tomato puree. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the red wine vinegar. Scrape up any bits from the base of the pan.
Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return the beef to the pot. The liquid should come halfway up the meat. Top up with water if needed.
Bring to the boil. Put the lid on and reduce to a very low simmer.
Cook for 2 to 2.5 hours, turning the beef once halfway through, until it falls apart easily.
Remove the beef. Shred it into the sauce using two forks.
Remove the herb sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving some pasta water.
Toss the pasta in the ragu with a little pasta water and serve immediately.

items.symptom: Beef is still tough after 2 hours.
items.cause: The heat was too high and the meat toughened rather than braised.
items.fix: Keep the liquid at a bare simmer and cook for a further 30 minutes.

items.symptom: Sauce is thin and lacks body.
items.cause: Too much liquid was added or the lid was on the whole time.
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 30 minutes to reduce the sauce.
